tracks.narration: Two inputs, one output — so which slope are we even talking about?
Here is a surface z equals f of x and y. To talk about slope, freeze one input. Hold y at one fixed value — the surface intersected with that plane is a single curve in x and z.
Sweep the slice plane through different y values. Each y gives its own curve. The slope of that curve at the chosen x is the partial derivative of f with respect to x.
Now swap roles. Freeze x at x zero and slice the surface the other way. The intersection curve runs along y, and its slope is the partial derivative of f with respect to y.
Two slopes through the same point — one along each axis. Together they make the gradient. Slicing was the whole trick.
